# Core Power 10Q Webscraping Script

```{r}
#| label: packages
# load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(robotstxt)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(quantmod)
library(dygraphs)
library(glue)
library(plotly)
library(paletteer)
library(ggrepel)
library(httr)
library(tidytext)
```

```{r}
#| label: importing-data

paths_allowed("https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872425000123/amzn-20250930.htm")

# FILD-D: Filing Date
```

## Scraping Script – Can be found as separate R file in alisha-xu-files

```{r}
#| eval: false
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This is the code for scraping 10Qs from HTM files from the SEC website
# for Microsoft, Google, Meta, Apple, Nvidia, and Tesla
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# packages
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(robotstxt)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(httr)


# import dataset 
# variable Explanations:
# COMP: Company Name
# FILD-D: Filing Date
# REP-D: Reporting For Date
# HTML: HTML link

ten_Qs <- readxl::read_xlsx("data/10q-links.xlsx")

# compartmentalize each variable
# Microsoft
microsoft <- ten_Qs |>
  filter(COMP == "Microsoft")

# Google
google <- ten_Qs |>
  filter(COMP == "Google")

# Meta
meta <- ten_Qs |>
  filter(COMP == "Meta")

# Apple
apple <- ten_Qs |>
  filter(COMP == "Apple")

# Nvidia
nvidia <- ten_Qs |>
  filter(COMP == "Nvidia")

# Tesla
tesla <- ten_Qs |>
  filter(COMP == "Tesla")

# create sec session
my_ua <- "AmherstCollege alxu27@amherst.edu"
sec_session <- session("https://www.sec.gov", user_agent(my_ua))

# add empty column to store values
ten_Qs <- ten_Qs |>
  mutate(RD = NA)

# -------------------------------Scraping---------------------------------------
# Microsoft
for (i in 1:4) {
  ten_Qs$RD[i] <- session_jump_to(sec_session, microsoft$HTML[i]) |>
    read_html() |>
    html_elements("table") |>
    purrr::pluck(7) |>
    html_table() |>
    filter(X1 == "Research and development") |>
    select(X4)
}

# Google
for (i in 1:2) {
  ten_Qs$RD[i+4] <- session_jump_to(sec_session, google$HTML[i]) |>
    read_html() |>
    html_elements("table") |>
    purrr::pluck(14) |>
    html_table() |>
    filter(X1 == "Research and development") |>
    select(X10)
}

for (i in 1:2) {
  ten_Qs$RD[i+6] <- session_jump_to(sec_session, google$HTML[i+2]) |>
    read_html() |>
    html_elements("table") |>
    purrr::pluck(15) |>
    html_table() |>
    filter(X1 == "Research and development") |>
    select(X10)
}  

# Meta
for (i in 1:4) {
  ten_Qs$RD[i+8] <- session_jump_to(sec_session, meta$HTML[i]) |>
    read_html() |>
    html_elements("table") |>
    purrr::pluck(7) |>
    html_table() |>
    filter(X1 == "Research and development") |>
    select(X4)
}

# third one
ten_Qs$RD[11] <- session_jump_to(sec_session, meta$HTML[3]) |>
  read_html() |>
  html_elements("table") |>
  purrr::pluck(7) |>
  html_table() |>
  filter(X1 == "Research and development") |>
  select(X16)

# Apple
for (i in 1:4) {
  ten_Qs$RD[i+12] <- session_jump_to(sec_session, apple$HTML[i]) |>
    read_html() |>
    html_elements("table") |>
    purrr::pluck(13) |>
    html_table() |>
    filter(X1 == "Research and development") |>
    select(X4)
}

# Nvidia
for (i in 1:4) {
  ten_Qs$RD[i+16] <- session_jump_to(sec_session, nvidia$HTML[i]) |>
    read_html() |>
    html_elements("table") |>
    purrr::pluck(8) |>
    html_table() |>
    filter(X1 == "Research and development") |>
    select(X4)
}

# Tesla
for (i in 1:4) {
  ten_Qs$RD[i+20] <- session_jump_to(sec_session, tesla$HTML[i]) |>
    read_html() |>
    html_elements("table") |>
    purrr::pluck(11) |>
    html_table() |>
    filter(X1 == "Research and development") |>
    select(X4)
}

ten_Qs_RD <- ten_Qs |>
  select(!HTML)

# convert RD column into numeric type column
ten_Qs_RD <- ten_Qs_RD |>
mutate(
  RD_clean = str_remove_all(RD, "[$, ]"), 
  RD = as.numeric(RD_clean)
) |>
  select(!RD_clean)

# export
write_csv(ten_Qs_RD, "data/scraped-10qs.csv")


```

## Stock Time Series

```{r}
#| label: stock-time-series

# copied from Sally's code
# grabbing closing price stock data for our companies from 3/1/25 to 11/1/26
microsoft_stock <- getSymbols("MSFT", src = "yahoo", from = "2025-03-01", to = "2026-11-01") |>
  data.frame(Date = index(MSFT), coredata(MSFT)) |>
  select(Date, MSFT.Close) |>
  rename(Close = MSFT.Close) |>
  mutate(COMP = "MSFT")

alphabet_stock <- getSymbols("GOOG", src = "yahoo", from = "2025-03-01", to = "2026-11-01") |>
  data.frame(Date = index(GOOG), coredata(GOOG)) |>
  select(Date, GOOG.Close) |>
  rename(Close = GOOG.Close) |>
  mutate(COMP = "GOOG")

meta_stock <- getSymbols("META", src = "yahoo", from = "2025-03-01", to = "2026-11-01") |>
  data.frame(Date = index(META), coredata(META)) |>
  select(Date, META.Close) |>
  rename(Close = META.Close) |>
  mutate(COMP = "META")

apple_stock <- getSymbols("AAPL", src = "yahoo", from = "2025-03-01", to = "2026-11-01") |>
  data.frame(Date = index(AAPL), coredata(AAPL)) |>
  select(Date, AAPL.Close) |>
  rename(Close = AAPL.Close) |>
  mutate(COMP = "AAPL")

nvidia_stock <- getSymbols("NVDA", src = "yahoo", from = "2025-03-01", to = "2026-11-01") |>
  data.frame(Date = index(NVDA), coredata(NVDA)) |>
  select(Date, NVDA.Close) |>
  rename(Close = NVDA.Close) |>
  mutate(COMP = "NVDA")

tesla_stock <- getSymbols("TSLA", src = "yahoo", from = "2025-03-01", to = "2026-11-01") |>
  data.frame(Date = index(TSLA), coredata(TSLA)) |>
  select(Date, TSLA.Close) |>   
  rename(Close = TSLA.Close) |>
  mutate(COMP = "TSLA")

all_days <- seq(start(AAPL), end(AAPL), by = "day") |>
  as_tibble_col("Date")

# one iteration test
microsoft_all_days <- microsoft_stock |>
  merge(all_days, by = "Date", all = TRUE) |>
  # LOCF
    fill(Close, COMP)



```

## Summary Tables

```{r}
#| label: summary-statistics-table

# stock price
microsoft_summary <- microsoft_stock |>
  summarise(
    "Mean" = mean(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "Median"= median(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "St. Dev." = sd(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(Company = "Microsoft") |>
  relocate(Company)

alphabet_summary <- alphabet_stock |>
  summarise(
    "Mean" = mean(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "Median"= median(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "St. Dev." = sd(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(Company = "Alphabet (Google)") |>
  relocate(Company)

meta_summary <- meta_stock |>
  summarise(
    "Mean" = mean(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "Median"= median(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "St. Dev." = sd(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(Company = "Meta") |>
  relocate(Company)

nvidia_summary <- nvidia_stock |>
  summarise(
    "Mean" = mean(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "Median"= median(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "St. Dev." = sd(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(Company = "Nvidia") |>
  relocate(Company)

apple_summary <- apple_stock |>
  summarise(
    "Mean" = mean(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "Median"= median(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "St. Dev." = sd(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(Company = "Apple") |>
  relocate(Company)

tesla_summary <- tesla_stock |>
  summarise(
    "Mean" = mean(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "Median"= median(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
    , "St. Dev." = sd(Close, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(Company = "Tesla") |>
  relocate(Company)

# join tables
stock_summary <- microsoft_summary |>
  full_join(alphabet_summary) |>
  full_join(meta_summary) |>
  full_join(nvidia_summary) |>
  full_join(apple_summary) |>
  full_join(tesla_summary)

stock_summary |> kable(digits = 2
                       , caption = "Company Stock Price Summary Statistics"
                       , format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Interactive Graphs

```{r}
#| label: interactive-graphs-sally's-code
#| eval: false
#| echo: false

# working on making visualizations interactive

scraped_ten_Qs <- read_csv("data/scraped-10qs.csv")

# Ensuring that company name formats conform between scraped 10-Qs and stock 
# price data set
companies <- 
  tibble(name1 = c("Apple", "Google", "Meta", "Microsoft", "Nvidia", "Tesla"),
         name2 = c("AAPL", "GOOG", "META", "MSFT", "NVDA", "TSLA"))
named_ten_Qs <- scraped_ten_Qs |> left_join(companies, by = c("COMP" = "name1"))

# To create accurate time series visualization elements (vertical lines for 
# 10-Q report dates and labels for corresponding quarterly R&D expenses)
vertical_lines <- named_ten_Qs |>
  select(name2, "REP-D") |>
  rename(COMP = "name2", reported_date = "REP-D")

text_labels <- named_ten_Qs |>
  select(name2, "REP-D", RD) |>
  rename(COMP = "name2", reported_date = "REP-D") |>
  mutate(x_position = reported_date - days(5), 
         y_position = 1000,
         text_values = glue("Quarterly R&D Expense: {named_ten_Qs$RD}   
                            million"))

# ggplot
ggplot(data=stock_price_joined, aes(x = Date, y = Close)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~COMP) +
  geom_vline(data=vertical_lines, aes(xintercept = reported_date))

```

```{r}
#| label: my-code
# -----------------------------Alisha Xu Work-----------------------------------
# AAPL and NVDA report on Saturdays, when there is no closing price, so we have to take the price for the previous day

# from = "2025-03-01", to = "2026-11-01"
all_days <- seq(start(AAPL), end(AAPL), by = "day") |>
  as_tibble_col("Date")

# using tidyverse fill() function to fill missing data for all companies
companies <- c("microsoft", "alphabet", "meta", "apple", "nvidia", "tesla")
for (i in companies) {
  df <- get(paste0(i,"_stock")) |>
  merge(all_days, by = "Date", all = TRUE) |>
  # LOCF
  fill(Close, COMP)
  
  assign(paste0(i, "_all_days"), df)
}

stock_price_joined <- bind_rows(microsoft_all_days, alphabet_all_days, meta_all_days, apple_all_days, nvidia_all_days, tesla_all_days)

# editing this variable to include closing price
text_labels <- named_ten_Qs |>
  select(name2, "REP-D", RD) |>
  rename(COMP = "name2", REPD = "REP-D") |>
  left_join(stock_price_joined
             , join_by(COMP, REPD == Date)) |>
  mutate(y_position = c(
    # MSFT
    700, 600, 700, 600,
    # GOOG
    700, 600, 700, 600, 
    # META
    300, 200, 300, 200,
    # AAPL
    700, 600, 700, 600,
    # NVDA
    700, 600, 700, 600,
    # TSLA
    700, 600, 700, 600
  ), 
  x_offset = 30)



# ggplot
ts_visual <- ggplot(data=stock_price_joined
                    , aes(
                      x = Date
                      , y = Close
                      , color = COMP)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~COMP) +
  scale_color_paletteer_d("MetBrewer::Archambault") +
  geom_point(data=text_labels
             , aes(x = REPD
                 , y = Close)) +  
  geom_vline(data=vertical_lines
             , aes(xintercept = reported_date)
             , linetype = 2
             , color = "#1e5977") +
  geom_label(data=text_labels
            , aes(
              x = REPD
              , y = y_position
              , label = paste(REPD,
                              "\n$", RD)
              , nudge_x = 15
            )
            , size = 2
            , hjust = "left"
            ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ts_visual
ggplotly(ts_visual)

```

## Text Analysis Review

```{r}
#| label: text-analysis-scraping

ten_Qs_text <- readxl::read_xlsx("data/10q-links.xlsx")

# compartmentalize each variable
# Microsoft
microsoft <- ten_Qs_text |>
  filter(COMP == "Microsoft")

# Google
google <- ten_Qs_text |>
  filter(COMP == "Google")

# Meta
meta <- ten_Qs_text |>
  filter(COMP == "Meta")

# Apple
apple <- ten_Qs_text |>
  filter(COMP == "Apple")

# Nvidia
nvidia <- ten_Qs_text |>
  filter(COMP == "Nvidia")

# Tesla
tesla <- ten_Qs_text |>
  filter(COMP == "Tesla")

# create sec session
my_ua <- "AmherstCollege alxu27@amherst.edu"
sec_session <- session("https://www.sec.gov", user_agent(my_ua))

# add empty column to store values
ten_Qs_text_scraped <- ten_Qs_text |>
  mutate(text = NA)

# -------------------------------Scraping---------------------------------------
# Microsoft
for (i in 1:4) {
  all_text_microsoft <- session_jump_to(sec_session, microsoft$HTML[i]) |>
    read_html() |>
    html_elements("span") |>
    html_text2()
  
  detect_1 <- which(str_detect(all_text_microsoft, "ITEM 2. MANAGEMENT’S"))
  
  detect_2 <- which(str_detect(all_text_microsoft, "ITEM 3. QUANTITATIVE"))
  
  scraped_text_microsoft <- all_text_microsoft[detect_1:detect_2]
  
  ten_Qs_text_scraped$text[i] <- paste(scraped_text_microsoft, collapse = "/n") |>
                                   str_replace_all("/n", " ")
}

# Google
for (i in 1:4) {
  all_text_google <- session_jump_to(sec_session, google$HTML[i]) |>
    read_html() |>
    html_elements("span") |>
    html_text2()
  
  detect_1 <- which(str_detect(all_text_google, "MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS"))

  ten_Qs_text_scraped$text[i+4] <- paste(scraped_text_google, collapse = "/n") |>
                                      str_replace_all("/n", " ")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: text-analysis

#---------------------------------for review-----------------------------------------------------
afinn_lexicon <- get_sentiments("afinn")
nrc_lexicon <- get_sentiments("nrc")

data(stop_words)

# wrangled unnest tokens
ten_Qs_text_analysis <- ten_Qs_text_wrangled |>
  unnest_tokens(output = word, input = text) |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  filter(!str_detect(word, "\\d"))

# aggregate company sentiment across all reports
ten_Qs_sentiment_analysis_1 <- ten_Qs_text_wrangled |>
  unnest_tokens(output = word, input = text) |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  filter(!str_detect(word, "\\d")) |>
  inner_join(afinn_lexicon, by = "word") |>
  group_by(COMP) |>
  summarize(
    sentiment = mean(value))

# sentiment split up by company
ten_Qs_sentiment_analysis_2 <- ten_Qs_text_wrangled |>
  unnest_tokens(output = word, input = text) |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  filter(!str_detect(word, "\\d")) |>
  inner_join(afinn_lexicon, by = "word") |>
  group_by(document_id) |>
  summarize(
    sentiment = mean(value))

#text analysis by report
ten_Qs_text_analysis_3 <- ten_Qs_text_wrangled |>
  unnest_tokens(output = word, input = text) |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  filter(!str_detect(word, "\\d")) |>
  group_by(document_id) |>
  count(word) |>
  bind_tf_idf(term=word, document=document_id, n=n) |> 
  arrange(desc(tf))
```
